research_rows.subject: Alpha testing — March–April 2001
notes: The publisher closed alpha-monitor recruitment on March 23, 2001 after reaching its intended participant count. This establishes recruitment closure, not the alpha client’s first release date.
An April 11 notice scheduled the alpha edition to end on April 13 at 15:00. It provides no client build number and does not independently confirm completion at that time.

research_rows.subject: Open beta — April 16, 2001
notes: The April 11 publisher notice announces public beta access from April 16, 2001 at 15:00, explicitly distinguishing it from the limited alpha edition.
A same-day April 16 notice confirms beta downloads resumed after FTP congestion. This corroborates beta distribution that day; neither notice identifies a client version number.

research_rows.subject: Commercial service — September 4, 2001
notes: The August 6 publisher announcement schedules formal service for September 4. A September 4 notice explicitly confirms formal service began that day and the beta edition ended.
Beta character IDs remained usable. The publisher specifies 1,000 yen per month including tax for up to two characters, with characters below level 10 still free.
These service notices state no client version number. The commercial launch must not be assigned to 4.30 merely because it is the preceding documented numbered update.

research_rows.subject: 5.00 — July 25, 2002 introduction
notes: The July 24 publisher notice schedules the production upgrade from 4.52 for July 25. Its July 25 follow-up explicitly confirms Version 5.00 was introduced, maintenance finished and the full 5.00 client was available.
The February 19, 2003 notice independently identifies 5.00 as the current production client before 5.20. Vector’s earlier package-file date is not an authenticated production introduction date.
The June 25 public test distribution is a separate channel. Matching 5.00 labels do not establish identical test and production binaries; neither package was recovered in this news pass.

research_rows.subject: 5.00 — public test server
notes: The June 25, 2002 publisher notice explicitly says the 5.00 test server is open to anyone, free of charge, without a NEXON account. Production characters were copied from June 25 data; test changes would not carry back to production.
The publisher advertises Yami500T.exe at 65.3 MB, but these package bytes and size remain unverified. June 27 at 17:00 is the planned test closing time, not a confirmed completed shutdown.
The source calls this a test server rather than explicitly calling it beta. Keep it separate from production 5.00 introduced July 25 and from the June 28 soccer-event schedule.

research_rows.subject: 4.51 / 4.52 — introduction conflict
notes: The January 24, 2002 notice plans a 4.30 to 4.51 upgrade for late January or early February. February 5 and 6 notices instead schedule 4.52 for February 14, still naming 4.30 as current.

A preserved news index lists an unlinked February 14 headline saying the 4.52 patch distribution started; its full announcement body and article URL were not recovered. March 18 instead names 4.51 as current and March 19 confirms 4.52 introduction.

These sources do not establish whether the earlier schedule changed, the service reverted, or a version label was mistaken. The first 4.52 release date remains unknown; February 14 is retained as an earlier scheduled/index-reported date and March 19 as a confirmed introduction. Neither is silently selected as the first release.
The earlier 4.52 announcement lists changes relative to 4.30. Those planned changes are retained in the source record rather than merged into the later 4.51-relative changelog without qualification.

research_rows.subject: 4.52 — Japanese publisher testimony
notes: Nexon Japan’s February 6, 2002 notice explicitly says the Korean edition was already operating Version 4.52 ahead of Japan, with the same intermittent party/zero-HP defect.

This is direct cross-regional publisher testimony, not a recovered Korean release notice. It establishes availability by February 6, but gives no Korean first-release date, predecessor, complete changelog or production/test channel.

research_rows.subject: 2004 — service and gameplay changes
notes: The June 3, 2004 notice schedules an account-price reduction from 1,000 to 500 yen per month from July 1, retaining two characters per account. This is an announced pricing change, not a newly numbered client.

June 8 completed maintenance confirms accelerated skill-level growth. A later update that day corrects reduced spell-level caps for some classes. Neither notice states a client version number; these changes must not be assigned automatically to 5.22b.

research_rows.subject: 2005 — free access and closure schedule
notes: The July 1, 2005 publisher notice announces service closure for November 30 and free access beginning September 1. The November 30 date is an explicit shutdown schedule; a same-day completion notice was not recovered.

A September 1 notice confirms fees were set to free at 12:20 that day, with paid-service character data retained and previously unregistered characters allowed to log in. No new client version number is supplied.

research_rows.subject: Publisher date inconsistencies
notes: Notice74 prints 2001/02/26 amid surrounding 2002 notices and reports maintenance ended without changes. Preserve that literal header; it does not securely establish a February 2001 service or client milestone.

Noticeold103 prints 2002/04/30 while discussing the June screenshot winner and July voting. The old-news index dates that subject July 1. Neither the parsed header nor the Wayback capture date independently settles its publication day.

The broader archive review includes unnumbered fixes, maintenance, rollback, support changes and recurring events. Their existence is preserved in the full article review and must not be converted into invented client numbers.

research_rows.subject: Archived news — review coverage
notes: The October 14, 2026 follow-up queried both archived official Japanese hostnames and attempted all 333 observed news HTML paths, ten additional article links and two broken webzine links: 345 targets in total.

The usable captures include 198 article paths representing 154 distinct article texts, plus six index/navigation bodies. Every recovered article was read in full; duplicate copies are one work. The remaining 141 targets have explicit failure records.

This completes the observed linked/archive frontier, not every historical post or every saved revision. A missing body, index headline or capture timestamp must not be presented as a verified release date.

before.date_note: No explicit release day was recovered. File timestamps, filenames and Wayback capture dates are preservation evidence, not release dates.

after.date_note: The July 25 publisher notice confirms Version 5.00 was introduced; the June 25 test distribution is separate.
release_notes: Redesigned the status window; Ability and GP remained in development
Changed screenshot format from PCX to BMP
Improved Japanese text input and client stability

after.date_scope: first release unresolved between earlier schedule/index and later completed introduction
after.date_note: February 14 is an earlier announced/index-reported introduction; March 19 is a confirmed introduction. Conflicting current/predecessor labels prevent establishing the first release date.

added_record.date_scope: publisher availability bound; first release unknown
added_record.date_note: Japanese publisher testimony establishes Korean 4.52 operation by February 6, 2002; original Korean release date and production/test channel remain unknown
research_notes: Japanese publisher testimony establishes Korean 4.52 operation by February 6, 2002; original Korean release date and production/test channel remain unknown

coverage.scope: Every exact news HTML path produced by the retained official CDX inventories, fresh official-host queries, and in-scope links on every recovered page was attempted. This is an exhausted observed frontier, not all Japanese Yami news ever published or every Wayback snapshot.
coverage.host_alias_policy: The observed official hosts www.nexon.co.jp and gamewww.nexon.co.jp are grouped only by exact case-preserved path/query. Original scheme, host, port and capture rows remain in inventory.json; different news and noticeold paths are separate capture targets.

fresh_discovery.coverage_method: The www news prefix returned its complete page. Direct gamewww news and both noticeold prefix requests returned transient 503/timeout failures, retained verbatim. A fresh complete gamewww /yami/* parent query below its row limit supplies the entire observed news subset, including noticeold. The union reobserves all 333 retained prior news paths. No new CDX path was discovered.

limits: A CDX status-200 record is not proof that its body could be recovered in this session.
Body failures and error pages are retained only as failure evidence in data; no error page was catalogued as publisher content.
One full successful body per exact path was selected; meaningful alternate captures were tried when the body failed. This is not a review of every historical revision of every notice.
Images and linked client/patch binaries were not automatically recovered or executed.

The recovered old-news index has an unlinked February 14, 2002 Version 4.52 patch-distribution heading. No corresponding article URL or body was recovered. Neither notice72 path appears in the retained or fresh inventories or observed links, so that inferred article number must not be assigned as source metadata.
Printed publication-date conflicts are preserved. Notice74 prints 2001/02/26 amid 2002 notices; noticeold103 prints April 30 while describing June screenshot winners and July voting.
